values.headline: The 10-K and eleven calls
values.sub: Everything on screen is in one of those two documents

values.body: You pay per person who logs in, every month, whether or not they log in.
values.example: Four thousand depots, nine seats each, forty dollars a seat.

values.caption: The last box is the only one anybody argues about

values.title: WHAT WOULD MAKE IT STICKY
values.row-1: The dispatcher opens it before coffee
values.row-2: It holds the customer list nobody else has
values.row-3: Ripping it out costs a week of missed loads
values.caption: Three tests, and it passes two

values.detail-1: nine seats, forty dollars, every month
values.detail-2: included with the fleet contract they already signed
values.caption: You cannot out-price free, you can only out-last it

values.label: on the LTM
values.detail: a real software margin, priced like a reseller
values.caption: From the filing
One acquisition, three years of hiring, and a word

values.body: We are managing the business for durable growth rather than for any single quarter's margin.
We think the right measure of this business is annual recurring revenue, not GAAP revenue, and we would encourage you to look at it that way.

values.headline: Tested on trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA
values.sub: Not on EBITDA. On adjusted EBITDA, as defined in the agreement.

values.body: Our credit agreement contains a covenant tested on trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, and we may not remain in compliance.

values.label: of float, and rising
values.detail: up from six percent a year ago
values.caption: Borrow is still cheap, which tells you something
Ten years of that, and it is a gut-check, not a fair value
It has been cheaper than this, twice
The same business, at the price it traded at two years ago

values.statement-1: Forty percent of revenue is contracted.
values.detail-1: Churn is falling, and the new CFO stopped buying growth in March.
values.statement-2: One point four billion of debt.
values.detail-2: Four hundred million of cash, and share count up six percent a year.
values.caption: Both of these are true at the same time

values.title: THREE QUESTIONS
values.row-1: Does the cash come back, and when
values.row-2: Who has to be wrong for this to work
values.row-3: What would make me sell it in a month
values.caption: If I can't answer the third one, I don't own it

values.line-1: The business is better than the chart.
values.line-2: The balance sheet is worse than the story.
values.line-3: You don't have to swing at every pitch.

values.statement-1: Sales and marketing down twenty percent, revenue flat.
values.detail-1: That would mean they were overspending and stopped.
values.statement-2: The renewal number back in the disclosure.
values.detail-2: You do not put a number back unless it improved.
values.caption: Two things, both checkable, both in the next two filings
